predecessors.name: Tughlaq dynasty
predecessors.text: the province of Jaunpur, whose governor Malik Sarwar 'established himself as an independent ruler' soon after 1394

successors.name: Lodi dynasty
successors.text: the Sharqi rump in the east after Hussain Shah's defeat at Benares in 1494 (Cliopatria's Lodi 1497 step), the core having gone to Bahlul Lodi in 1479

successors.name: Bengal Sultanate
successors.text: the Bihar block: Bengal's 1352 shape minus its 1395 shape (Patna to Darbhanga)

ledger.x: 1394: Malik Sarwar founds the Jaunpur Sultanate.
Malik Sarwar's early gains are undated: he 'suppressed rebellions in Etawah, Koil, and Kanauj' and controlled Kara, Awadh, Dalmau, Bahraich and South Bihar; 1395 is Cliopatria's first year.
Malik Sarwar 'was also able to bring under his control Kara, Awadh, Dalmau, Bahraich and South Bihar' (no year, no previous holder named).
1420: 'Parts of the Jaunpur Sultanate were annexed by Bengal, and peace was established between the two states.'
1420: the war ends in peace between the two states.
1457: Muhammad Shah 'made peace with Bahlul and recognised his right over Shamsabad'.
1458: Hussain Shah 'signed a four-year peace treaty with Bahlul Lodi'.
1479: the final defeat on the Rahab after battles at Senha, Rapri and Raigaon Khaga; the last dated Sharqi inscription in Jaunpur.
March 1479: Hussain 'returned to the Yamuna, was defeated again, and lost the parganas of Kampil, Patiali, Shamsabad, Suket, Koil, Marhara, and Jalesar'.
1482: the south-bank part of the Bihar block passes to Bengal in Cliopatria's 1482 step; no page dates it.

wars.name: Bengal-Jaunpur War
wars.outcome: 'Parts of the Jaunpur Sultanate were annexed by Bengal' (Bengal page, no place named; read as Tirhut north of the Ganga).

wars.name: Lodi-Sharqi War
wars.outcome: 1452 Mahmud Shah besieges Delhi and loses; 1457 Shamsabad conceded; 1458 four-year peace; 1478 and March 1479 defeats on the Yamuna cost seven parganas and the core of the realm (Bahlul 'annexed' it in 1479); Hussain Shah re-occupies Jaunpur for a time, is…

wars.name: Odia (Gajapati) war with Jaunpur
wars.outcome: The Jaunpur page says 'Kapilendra Deva's Odia forces defeated Jaunpur' without a year; the Kapilendra Deva page has the second Jaunpur invasion of Orissa 'in 1458 by Husain Shah' and links it to the Gajapati withdrawal from the 1461 Berar campaign.

wars.name: Sharqi invasion of Delhi
wars.outcome: Ibrahim Shah Sharqi 'annexed large parts of the Delhi Sultanate and besieged Delhi'; Muhammad Shah 'sought for peace and offered a matrimonial alliance', his daughter Bibi Raji marrying Ibrahim's son Mahmud Khan.

certainty.note: No treaty line is recorded; the 1458 four-year peace did not fix a boundary on the page.
